title: tests/store/tracking conftest: reuse the root session cached_db instead of redefining a module-scoped copy
answers: Why did the tracking store test module stop defining its own cached_db fixture?
My tracking store tests run migrations once per module and use a shared artifact_folder, what should I do?
Where does the tracking store test fixture get its SQLite database from now?
body:
Path: tests/store/tracking/conftest.py:store builds a SqlAlchemyStore per test from the cached_db fixture, which now comes from the root tests/conftest.py rather than a module override.
Rule: Do not redefine a module-scoped cached_db in tests/store/tracking/conftest.py. The root session-scoped cached_db is schema-only and reused across modules, so migrations run once per session. Per-test artifact paths should come from tmp_path (as the store fixture does), not from a shared relative path such as "artifact_folder".
Symptom: Each tracking test module ran its own migrations and wrote artifacts to a relative artifact_folder shared across tests, which made tests slower and let runs collide.
Constraints: This covers the tracking store test package only; other test packages that need a different database setup should keep their own fixtures.
applies: Tracking store tests under tests/store/tracking/; applies when adding or editing fixtures there that need a SQLite database.
says: Tracking test suite runs slowly and concurrent test runs collide over shared artifacts
Speed up tracking tests by preventing redundant database migrations across test modules

This applies when adding or editing fixtures needing a SQLite database in tests/store/tracking, while other test packages needing different database setups keep their own fixtures.
